title: Fold-in
rule: Folding the page along its marked lines hides the interruption and joins departure to cupboard, making a story in which he remembers.
declares: the folded reading is a marked alternate (outcome changed only when folded)
build: films/swarm/99-ways/build/p80_fold_in.py (busch-fold kit: build/p59_once_upon.py, p39_meanwhile.py, p11_station_cat.py, p69_picture_sheet.py)

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

made: the sheet (les-caids vintage paper on the les-caids wood table) ruled by two red dashed fold lines A (x 770) and B (x 1430), lettered A/B top and bottom, with an A-to-B arrow

head: 'FOLD-IN' | the question in the hidden strip | the folding instructions; the headline 'WHAT HE | CAME FOR, HE FOR | GETS' set so that unfolded it reads 'WHAT HE CAME FOR, HE FORGETS' and folded 'WHAT HE GETS'

three wide tiers in the HANDMADE ink set with the les-caids porter cutout (Busch 1865) as the agent: T1 desk and memo | clock | he walks off; T2 he crosses | the ticket window with Helene (Busch 1872) behind the glass, clock 4:10, question, answer and thanks balloons | on to the cupboard; T3 the open cupboard door (left jamb) with the brass key on its hook and SERVICE tag | the dark inside and the forgetting balloon | the agent, pencil to chin, a HANDMADE reaching arm whose fingertips stop exactly at line B, the SERVICE door shut

tier captions written for both readings: L text on the first row, the hidden strip's rows, R text on the last row; unfolded they keep the canon ('...Nobody takes it.'), folded they close up into 'So off he goes for the key.' / 'Across the office he goes, and on he goes, to the cupboard.' / 'He opens it, sees the key, and takes it.'
foot: 'Fold so that A meets B.' | 'Unfolded, it is what happened.' | 'Folded, it is what he came for.'; folio '80 / Fold-in'

events.E2: T2 middle strip: clock 4:10, answer balloon
events.E4: T3 left strip: cupboard open, key on its hook
events.E5: T3 middle strip: forgetting balloon; caption 'The key stays on its hook; the SERVICE door stays shut. Nobody takes it.'

beat: the sheet folded on the table: the middle strip folds back and closes up until A meets B; the folded sheet shows the hand on the key and 'WHAT HE GETS'

self_check.check: Unfolded the page keeps the canon; folded it shows the agent taking the key.
self_check.evidence: perceptually judged by the maker from the full-size page; blind reading pending

weaknesses: the reaching arm and hand are crude HANDMADE ink against Busch's line; unfolded the arm reads as a long reach that stops short, which is the point but looks odd
folded, the hand touches the key's bow rather than closing round it; the caption 'and takes it' does the rest
the folded state is not on the still page itself (only in the beats); the reader must fold to see it
T2's middle strip is crowded: three small balloons (cap 24) over the window and clock, small at phone width
in the folded rows the R caption sits one or two rows below the L caption (blank rows between)
